sanskrit: prāṇo mṛtyuḥ prāṇo amṛtaṃ prāṇaṃ devā upāsate | prāṇo ha satyavādinam uttame loka ā dadhat ||
english: Prāṇa is death; prāṇa is immortality; the gods attend upon prāṇa. Prāṇa indeed establishes the truth-speaker in the highest world.

sanskrit: prāṇo virāṭ prāṇo deṣṭrī prāṇaṃ sarvā upāsate | prāṇo 'gniś candramāḥ sūryaḥ prāṇam āhuḥ prajāpatim ||
english: Prāṇa is Virāj; prāṇa is the directress; all things attend upon prāṇa. Prāṇa is Agni, the moon, the sun; they call prāṇa Prajāpati.

sanskrit: prāṇāpānau vrīhayavāv anaḍvān prāṇa ucyate | yave ha prāṇa āhito apāno vrīhir ucyate ||
english: Prāṇa and apāna are rice and barley; the ox is called prāṇa. In barley indeed prāṇa is lodged; apāna is called rice.

sanskrit: apānati prāṇati puruṣo garbhe antaḥ | yadā tvaṃ prāṇa jinvasy atha sa jāyate tvat ||
english: The person breathes out and breathes in while yet within the womb. When thou, O Prāṇa, dost quicken him, then he is born forth from thee.

sanskrit: prāṇam āhur mātariśvānaṃ vāto ha prāṇa ucyate | prāṇe ha bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ ca prāṇe sarvaṃ samāhitam ||
english: They call prāṇa Mātariśvan; wind indeed is called prāṇa. In prāṇa verily are the past and the future; in prāṇa is all things gathered together.

sanskrit: ātharvaṇīr āṅgirasīr daivīr manuṣyajāś ca yāḥ | sarvāḥ pra modanta oṣadhīr yadā tvaṃ prāṇa jinvasi ||
english: The plants of Atharvan, those of the Āṅgirases, the divine ones, and those born among men — all plants rejoice when thou, O Prāṇa, dost quicken them.

sanskrit: yadā prāṇo abhyavarṣīd varṣeṇa pṛthivīṃ mahīm | oṣadhayaḥ pra modante atho yāḥ kāś ca vīrudhaḥ ||
english: When Prāṇa has rained upon the great earth with rain, the plants rejoice, and likewise whatsoever creeping herbs there are.

sanskrit: yas te prāṇedaṃ veda yasmiṃś cāsi pratiṣṭhitaḥ | sarve asmai baliṃ harān amuṣmiṃl loka uttame ||
english: Whoever knows this thy prāṇa and that in which thou art established — may all things bring tribute to him in yonder highest world.

sanskrit: yathā prāṇa balihṛtas tubhyaṃ sarvāḥ prajā imāḥ | evā tasmai baliṃ harān yas tvā śuśrāva śuśruvuḥ ||
english: As, O Prāṇa, all these creatures here bring tribute to thee, so may they bring tribute to him who has heard thee, to those who have heard.

sanskrit: antargarbhaś carati devatāsv ābhūto bhūtaḥ sa u jāyate punaḥ | sa bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhaviṣyat pitā putraṃ pra viveśā śacībhiḥ ||
english: He moves within the womb among the gods; having come into being he is born again. He — the past, the future, the world, the yet-to-be — as a father has entered the son by his powers.

sanskrit: ekaṃ padaṃ not khidati salilād dhaṃsa utpatan | yad aṅga sa tam utkhiden naivādya na śvo na rātrī nāhaḥ syān na prajñāyaiti kiṃ cana ||
english: The swan does not wrench up even one foothold as it flies up from the water. If, O friend, he were to wrench it up, then there would be neither today nor tomorrow, neither night nor day, nor would anything whatsoever be discerned.

sanskrit: aṣṭācakraṃ vartata ekanemi sahasrākṣaraṃ pra puro ni paścāt | ardhenedaṃ pari babhūva viśvaṃ yad asyārdhaṃ katamaḥ sa ketuḥ ||
english: Eight-wheeled it rolls, single-rimmed, with a thousand syllables, onward in front and backward behind. By its half has this whole universe come into being; what then is that half — what is its sign?

sanskrit: yo asya viśvajanmana īśe sarvasya ceṣṭataḥ | anyeṣu kṣipradhanvane tasmai prāṇa namo 'stu te ||
english: He who is lord of this universe of all beings, who moves all things — among the others, to the swift-bowed one: to him, O Prāṇa, be homage to thee.

sanskrit: yo asya sarvajanmana īśe viśvasya ceṣṭataḥ | atandro brahmaṇā dhīraḥ prāṇo mām abhi rakṣatu ||
english: He who is lord of all the beings of this universe, who moves all things — may Prāṇa, unwearied, wise with brahman, protect me.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaḥ supteṣu jāgāra nanu tīryaṅ ni padyate | na suptam asya supteṣv anu śuśrāva kaś cana ||
english: Standing upright he keeps watch among the sleeping; he does not lie crosswise. Of his sleeping among the sleepers no one has ever heard.

sanskrit: prāṇa mā mat paryāvṛto na mad anyo bhaviṣyasi | apāṃ garbham iva jīvase prāṇa badhnāmi tvā mayi ||
english: O Prāṇa, do not turn away from me; thou shalt be no other than me. Like the embryo of the waters, for life I bind thee within me, O Prāṇa.

sanskrit: sāhasras tveṣa ṛṣabhaḥ payasvān viśvā rūpāṇi vakṣaṇāsu bibhrat | bhadraṃ dātre yajamānāya śikṣan bārhaspatya usriyas tantum ātān ||
english: This bull of a thousand, rich in milk, bearing all forms upon his flanks, teaching welfare to the giver and the sacrificer — he, son of Bṛhaspati, has stretched the thread of the dawn-cows.

sanskrit: apāṃ yo agre pratimā babhūva prabhūḥ sarvasmai pṛthivīva devī | pitā vatsānāṃ patir aghnyānāṃ sāhasre poṣe api naḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: He who at the first became the measure of the waters, lord over all like the divine earth — the father of calves, the master of the inviolable cows, may he place us in thousandfold nourishment.

sanskrit: pumān antarvān sthaviraḥ payasvān vasoḥ kabandham ṛṣabho bibharti | tam indrāya pathibhir devayānair hutam agnir vahatu jātavedāḥ ||
english: A male, pregnant, ancient, rich in milk — the bull bears the barrel of treasure. May Agni Jātavedas carry him, offered up by the paths that lead to the gods, to Indra.

sanskrit: devānāṃ bhāga upanāha eṣo apāṃ rasa oṣadhīnāṃ ghṛtasya | somasya drapsam avṛṇīta śakro bṛhann adrir abhavad yac charīram ||
english: This is the portion of the gods, the binding-bond, the essence of waters, of plants, of clarified butter. Śakra chose the drop of Soma; the great stone-presser became what is his body.

sanskrit: pitā vatsānāṃ patir aghnyānām atho pitā mahatāṃ gargarāṇām | vatso jarāyuḥ pratidhuk pīyūṣa āmikṣā ghṛtaṃ tad v asya retaḥ ||
english: Father of calves, lord of the inviolable cows, and moreover father of the great bellowing bulls — the calf is the afterbirth; the beestings are the first milking; curds, clarified butter — that indeed is his seed.

sanskrit: somasya pūrṇaṃ kalaśaṃ bibharṣi tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāṃ janitā paśūnām | śivās te santu prajanva imā ny asmabhyaṃ svadhite yaccha yā amūḥ ||
english: Thou bearest a full vessel of Soma; Tvaṣṭṛ, the begetter of forms, the progenitor of cattle — may thy generative powers be propitious; grant us those yonder ones, O self-powerful one.

sanskrit: indrasyaujo varuṇasya bāhū aśvinor aṃsau marutām iyaṃ kakut ||
english: The vigor of Indra, the arms of Varuṇa, the shoulders of the Aśvins — this is the hump of the Maruts.

sanskrit: ājyaṃ bibharti ghṛtam asya retaḥ sāhasraḥ poṣas tam u yajñam āhuḥ | indrasya rūpam ṛṣabho vasānaḥ so asmāṃ devāḥ śiva aitu dattaḥ ||
english: He bears the oblation-butter; clarified butter is his seed; thousandfold nourishment — that they call the sacrifice. Wearing the form of Indra, may this bull, given by the gods, come to us benignly.

sanskrit: daivīr viśaḥ payasvān ā tanoṣi tvām indraṃ tvāṃ sarasvantam āhuḥ | sahasraṃ sa ekamukhā dadāti yo brāhmaṇa ṛṣabham ā juhoti ||
english: Rich in milk, thou stretchest out the divine clans; they call thee Indra, they call thee Sarasvant. A thousand at a single bestowal does he give who sacrifices a bull to a brahmin.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiḥ savitā te mano dadhau tvaṣṭur vāyoḥ pary ātmā ta ābhṛtaḥ | antarikṣe manasā tvā juhomi barhiṣ ṭe dyāvāpṛthivī abhūtām ||
english: Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ has established thy mind; thy breath of life has been brought from Tvaṣṭṛ and Vāyu. With mind I offer thee into the atmosphere; Heaven and Earth have become thy sacrificial grass.
